problem: Existing navigation systems rely on task- or embodiment-specific components (waypoint predictors, topological maps, separate action heads or diffusion/flow experts) that fragment perception, reasoning and action and do not exploit the spatial priors of pretrained VLMs. Discrete-token action interfaces are coarse, while continuous heads sit outside the language model and make RL awkward.
motivation: Modern VLMs already encode grounding, pointing and spatial reasoning, but these are rarely elicited directly for robot control. A shared, embodiment-agnostic intermediate representation plus a precise yet token-based action interface could let one compact VLM handle instruction following, object search and tracking across robots.
key_idea: Have a compact Qwen3-VL-4B emit dual-channel image-grid pointing tokens (affordance + object) as a latent spatial trace, followed by three residual-VQ tokens that decode to 10 SE(2) waypoints, all through the original LM head, trained with ER mid-training, SFT+DAgger and GRPO RL.
insight: Pointing supervision is the main driver: removing affordance/object point supervision drops mean SR from 63.0 to 54.7 and mean SPL from 39.9 to 34.3 over 8 settings (biggest on HM3D v1, +13.5 SR). ER initialization gives a consistent SR gain in all 8 settings (mean 60.5 to 63.0). Scaling: 4B is the sweet spot (8B mixed), and environment diversity is the most reliable scaling axis versus data volume, which saturates.
method: Dual-channel pointing: one affordance token <apos_i> and one object token <opos_i> on a shared image grid (reserved indices for turn/stop/invisible), serving as a fixed-length spatial reasoning prefix

RVQ action tokenizer: 3 levels x 256 codewords encode a 10-waypoint SE(2) trajectory (Jacobian-weighted residual k-means, ADE 0.72 cm vs 2.48 cm for a K=4096 single-level vocabulary); any prefix decodes to an executable trajectory, allowing early stopping
Temporally aware visual history compression: exponential-decay frame sampling and recency-dependent spatial pooling stride (Ebbinghaus-style) within 256K/576K/1M pixel budgets, with timestamp tokens
Staged training: ER mid-training on 36 sources yields LightNav-ER, then SFT on 16 navigation + 33 ER/VQA sources (77.6%/22.4%) with DAgger and camera randomization, then online GRPO RL

Online RL: group-relative advantage (G=8, B=32) with terminal task-specific rewards (EVT persistence-aware reward, VLN nDTW+Gaussian proximity, ObjNav path efficiency+proximity), mixed-difficulty episode filtering, event-stratified step subsampling; exact token log-probs since actions are LM tokens

INSIGHT-Bench and data pipeline: automatic multi-view pointing pre-annotation, rule/video-VLM instruction generation with checks; 1,683 train scenes/53,090 episodes and 210 eval scenes/1,097 episodes with a scene x instruction taxonomy
Deployment: vLLM inference (~4 ms/token on RTX 4090); shared trajectory follower converts waypoints to each robot's velocity commands

setting.training_data: ER mid-training (36 sources); SFT on 2K+ scenes / 4K+ hours navigation data (R2R, RxR, ScaleVLN, self-distilled routes, PIRLNav, HM3D, MP3D, VLNVerse, Habitat-GS, InteriorGS, HM3D-OVON, EVT-Bench, INSIGHT-Bench) plus 33 ER/VQA sources; DAgger; online GRPO RL
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB history (no depth, odometry, or panorama)
setting.action_space: 10 future SE(2) waypoints from 3 RVQ tokens, executed by an embodiment-specific low-level trajectory follower
setting.simulator: Habitat (VLN-CE, ObjectNav, OVON), EVT-Bench, plus game engines (CS 1.6, VizDoom, Minecraft, Trigger Rally) for qualitative tests
setting.privileged: none at test time (privileged oracle plan used only in RL reward for training)

numbers.extra: single shared checkpoint, monocular RGB, no depth/odometry
numbers.evidence: Tab. vln-ce, LightNav-0 row, R2R Val-Unseen

numbers.extra: monocular RGB only; unseen category split

numbers_note: EVT-Bench and INSIGHT-Bench splits are not official val/test names; 'test' used. ER benchmark results (LightNav-ER avg 67.4) are not navigation numbers and are omitted. Scaling results are given only in a figure with text values.
results: A single monocular 4B model achieves the best monocular SR across all 10 simulation settings, e.g. R2R-CE SR 68.5 (vs Qwen-RobotNav-4B 66.9), RxR-CE SR 73.6, HM3D-OVON large SPL gains, EVT DT SR 82.6 (vs ReferTrack 73.3). On INSIGHT-Bench it reaches 43.7 SR vs 27.4 for JanusVLN. LightNav-ER attains a 67.4 average over 8 ER benchmarks vs 63.1 for Qwen3-VL-4B.
limitations: Single decision pathway with no separation of fast reactive control from slow deliberation
Real-world and cross-domain evidence is qualitative only; panoramic methods still lead slightly in VLN and some tracking metrics (TR, nDTW) trail specialists
Open-world concept coverage limited by curated embodied data; 8B scaling did not help
